scope: Standalone generated public Boolean quadratic systems at <=24 variables. No curve inputs, imported targets, scalar recovery, production integration or rho workflow.
contract: Projection retains the first 16 equation coordinates exactly. Every projected zero is checked against the complete original system; false hits continue in the same assignment order. All hits/checks/rejections are counted. Caps produce UNKNOWN, never false UNSAT. Scalar-source and native 16/64-point representations share the same identities and compiled four-bit Gray schedule.
selection: Five fixed treatments: scalar-source and native 16/64-point blocks, plus native dispatch with 16-point blocks through n20 and 64-point blocks above. Scalar source may be auto-vectorized; no instruction-count claim. No coefficient-dependent output crosses systems.
accounting: Every arm charges a fresh complete cold solve including input validation and encoding, narrowing, schedule construction, scan, original-system hit checks and temporary-workspace release, plus external validation and repeat-signature checks. Returned diagnostic destruction, serialization and common fixture/reference preparation are outside arm clocks and inside worker receipts. No timing subtraction.
ordering: Four fixed Fisher-Yates permutations per fixture, each followed by its exact reverse.
boundary: The reference is the pointwise fastest of the 52 complete solvers retained before this experiment. New scalar/native variants are separate implementations of the same new representation, not independent older references. Native-vs-scalar attribution is reported separately. No calibrated operation conversion or cryptanalytic floor is measured.
decision: The complete-solve criterion is a paired 95 percent median-ratio lower bound >2.0 against the fastest retained reference in all 18 n16/n20/n24 x family x regression/holdout groups, with all cells complete and verified. Incremental >1.0 is separate. Any positive result requires unchanged-source confirmation on unused holdouts; no tuning after holdout timing.
encoding: One-pass domain validation and direct encoding of the first sixteen equation coordinates; omitted equations are still validated and used for every original-system check. No unsupported input silently falls back.
hardware_contract: Runtime SHA3 detection gates AArch64 EOR3 kernels. Both full 32-bit and projected 16-bit controls use the same three-input XOR operation. Unsupported hosts execute the matching portable XOR policy and report that capability; no hardware gain is inferred from fallback timings. No global target-cpu or target-feature override is used.
resource_contract: New timings require tools/isolated_bench.py with a reserved pinned CPU, per-worker resource records and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. A/A runs precede A/B. Contended, failed or missing-isolation observations are retained and do not enter eligible pooled timings. Builds/tests run through the busy lock before timed stages. Older probes are historical unisolated discovery evidence only.
noise_contract: Eight random/reverse A/A rounds compare two calls to the identical word_dispatch policy before A/B for every fixture. Report both ratios and the symmetric multiplicative spread. A paired performance lower bound must exceed the group A/A 97.5-percentile symmetric ratio in addition to its numeric threshold. No contended/uncontended pooling.
reference_scope: The 52 retained September 23 complete-solver implementations, rebuilt in the current same-binary image. This is a frozen reference roster, not a claim to cover every later repository optimization or all known solvers.
retention: Any refused, contended, timed-out or failed execution is sealed and retained. A later execution uses a new directory and is reported separately; no sample-level retries, seed replacement or pooling with unqualified data.
